endorsements.quote: The safe, practical, ethical, and sustainable operation of LASs will be informed by state-of-the-art implementation science incorporating clinician, patient, and public involvement.
Given the social impact of AMR, co-production of LASs with practitioners, patients, and the public is essential to ensure their operation is transparent, useful, and trustworthy.

unlisted_practices: Ensure ethical decisions where individual and societal benefits conflict are made by humans and not by algorithms.
Give patients access to their own clinical information and clear means to opt out of data collection.
Apply FAIR data procedures and prioritise data stewardship (privacy, transparency, security, governance) in learning antimicrobial systems.
Make code, algorithms and standard operating procedures of learning antimicrobial systems open-source and not monetised.
Legislate, vet, monitor and regulate private companies' access to healthcare data.
Clarify regulatory pathways for AI-based decision support algorithms such as model-informed precision dosing.
Clarify legal positions on data sharing and data protection impact assessment reflecting the public health impact of AMR.
Embed human-driven implementation science and governance in AI-enabled systems to provide accountability that AI cannot fulfil.

screen.reason: This is a Personal View / framework paper discussing antimicrobial treatment imprecision and how AI can support antimicrobial stewardship.
